measures.match: Match each unit to what it measures.
measures.odd: Three of these units measure {value}. Which one does not?

rows.label: parsec
rows.description: unit of length used in astronomy
rows.hook: is a favorite of astronomers and gets misused by Han Solo when bragging about the Kessel Run

rows.label: joule
rows.description: SI unit of energy, work and amount of heat
rows.hook: honors a British brewer's son who linked heat to motion, and shows up in kilo form on food labels

rows.label: light-year
rows.description: unit of astronomical length, defined as the distance that light travels in the vacuum in one year
rows.hook: is how astronomers describe how far away stars are, even though the name sounds like a span of time

rows.label: acre
rows.hook: was traditionally what a yoked pair of oxen could plough in a single day

rows.label: metre
rows.hook: was first defined as one ten-millionth of the way from the North Pole to the equator

rows.label: pascal
rows.description: SI unit of pressure and stress
rows.hook: honors a French polymath and is what tire gauges and weather barometers report

rows.label: hertz
rows.hook: honors the German physicist who proved radio waves exist, and is counted in cycles per second

rows.label: watt
rows.hook: honors the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine, and is printed on light bulbs and microwaves

rows.label: newton
rows.hook: honors the scientist said to have been inspired by a falling apple, and is roughly an apple's weight

rows.label: byte
rows.description: unit of digital information equal to 8 bits
rows.hook: is made of eight bits and is what the 'mega' and 'giga' on file sizes multiply

rows.label: knot
rows.hook: is used at sea and in the air, and once was counted by paying out a rope with knots behind a ship

rows.label: ampere
rows.hook: honors a French physicist and is what fuses and circuit breakers are rated in

rows.label: hectare
rows.hook: equals 10,000 square metres and is used for farmland and forests worldwide

rows.label: kilogram
rows.hook: is the only base unit with a prefix, and was long defined by a platinum-iridium cylinder in a Paris vault

rows.label: ohm
rows.description: SI derived unit of electrical resistance
rows.hook: honors a German physicist and is written with the Greek letter omega

rows.label: mile
rows.hook: began as a Roman count of a thousand paces and is still used on American road signs

rows.label: inch
rows.hook: was once defined as the width of a man's thumb, and equals 2.54 centimetres

rows.label: coulomb
rows.hook: honors a French physicist and is what flows when one amp runs for one second

rows.label: electronvolt
rows.hook: is used by particle physicists, with the Large Hadron Collider's beams counted in trillions of them

rows.label: bit
rows.description: basic unit of information in computing and digital communications
rows.hook: is a single 0 or 1, and eight of them make a byte

rows.label: tonne
rows.description: metric unit of mass equivalent to 1000 kilograms
rows.hook: equals a thousand kilograms and is spelled with an extra letter to tell it from the American ton

rows.label: volt
rows.description: SI unit of electric potential, of electric potential difference (voltage), and of electromotive force
rows.hook: honors the Italian inventor of the first battery, and is what wall outlets and AA batteries are rated in

rows.label: foot
rows.hook: is divided into twelve inches, and is how airplane altitudes are given

rows.label: lumen
rows.hook: is printed on light bulb boxes to say how bright they are

rows.label: litre
rows.description: unit of volume accepted for use with the SI
rows.hook: is roughly the size of a big soda bottle, equal to a thousand cubic centimetres
